title: Should XHR etc. still fire events after its document has gone inactive?
body:
See https://github.com/web-platform-tests/wpt/blob/a806d658df3bcc3f05675ad8d08a6e109177c6b0/xhr/open-url-multi-window-4.htm#L11-L17:

```js
    /*
    It's unclear what the pass condition should be for this test [which adds events listeners on
    XMLHttpRequest that belongs to a window that is no longer active].
    Implementations:
    Firefox, Opera (Presto): terminate request with no further events when IFRAME is removed.
    Chrome: completes request to readyState=4 but responseText is "" so it's pretty much terminated with an extra event for "DONE" state
    …
    */
```

The linked test current tests that an `error` event is fired for XHRs that are aborted due to its browsing context being discarded, a behavior only present in Safari.

After my planned change to Chrome to now fire `abort` event asynchronously (see https://crbug.com/879620), Chrome now has Firefox's behavior.

From IRC:

> <@annevk> @TimothyGu: so this depends on unspecced stuff
> <@annevk> @TimothyGu: how exactly canceling a fetch group looks
> <@annevk> @TimothyGu: if error events this would make sense, but dunno what would be best and what compat allows for
> <@annevk> s/looks/functions/
> <@TimothyGu> So Safari is the only one that does error events, per wpt.fyi (Edge result is missing though). A reasonable guess is that they only implemented that in order to fix this specific test.
> <@annevk> Yeah
> <@annevk> I guess the question is, when a doc goes inactive, how do all fetchy things behave today and does that match what we think is good
> <@annevk> Not firing events seems weird, but if you want to stop running code in a closed tab makes sense

Looping in @bzbarsky.

Cross filed at https://crbug.com/881180.
